contentSections: Every Indian homeowner knows the feeling. By 3 pm, the west wall is too hot to touch, the bedroom behind it feels like an oven, and the air conditioner runs flat out until late evening. If your plot or building faces west, that is not bad luck. It is physics, and it can be fixed with the right facade. This guide explains why west faces heat up so badly, and which facade, shading and finish choices make the biggest difference.

Why West Facing Walls Are the Hardest to Protect

In the afternoon, the sun sits low in the west. Its rays hit the wall almost straight on, and they come in at an angle that goes right under normal overhangs. By then, the wall and the surrounding air have already been heating up since morning. The result:

• The wall absorbs heat for hours and releases it into the room well into the night
  • Glass on the west side lets in strong, low angle sun and glare
  • Cooling load peaks exactly when the outdoor temperature is highest
A roof overhang or a plain horizontal canopy does little here, because the sun is too low. West faces need vertical protection and layered protection.
The 5 Facade Fixes That Work

1. Add an Outer Shading Layer

The best fix is to stop the sun before it reaches the wall or glass. A metal screen, fins or louvers set a short distance away from the building take the sun's heat first. The air gap behind carries away heat instead of letting it pass through. Vertical fins are especially effective on west faces, because they block low sun coming from the side. See our guide on architectural fins design and explore the MetaFin system.

2. Use Perforated or Mesh Screens

A perforated metal screen filters the sun through small openings. It cuts heat and glare, yet keeps some view and airflow. It also casts a beautiful pattern of light. Read more about the power of perforation.

3. Choose a Ventilated Facade

In a ventilated system, metal panels are fixed a few centimetres off the wall, leaving a cavity. Hot air rises and escapes through the cavity, so less heat reaches the wall behind. This is one of the best passive fixes for a west wall. Learn more in ventilated metal facade systems.

4. Reduce and Protect Glass

Glass is the weakest point on a west wall. Options include:

• Fewer or smaller west facing windows
  • Placing service rooms, stairs and storage on the west side
  • Deep recesses so windows sit in shade
  • Outer louvers or screens over the glass
  • Higher performance glass where windows are needed
See the MetaLouver range for louver options.

5. Pick Light Colours and Quality Finishes

Dark surfaces absorb more heat. Lighter colours reflect more sunlight and stay cooler. A durable finish also keeps its colour in strong sun. Our guide on PVDF vs powder coat explains how to choose a finish that lasts.
Fixed vs Movable Shading for West Faces

OptionStrengthTrade-off
Fixed vertical finsSimple, no upkeep, strong low sun controlReduces view at some angles
Fixed perforated screenCuts heat and glare, keeps some viewReduces daylight slightly
Movable fins or louversAdjust through day and seasonCost and mechanism upkeep
Ventilated claddingReduces wall heatDoes not shade glass by itself
For most Indian buildings, fixed fins or screens combined with ventilated cladding give the best balance.

Smart Layout Moves

Facade design is not only about materials. Planning helps too:

• Place bathrooms, stairs, store rooms and kitchens on the west side as heat buffers
  • Use deep balconies and terraces as shade for rooms behind
  • Plant trees on the west side where possible
  • Keep large living spaces and bedrooms away from the west wall

Heat, Climate and Material Choice

Different Indian cities add their own challenges, from dry heat to humidity and salt. Our article on designing for Indian climate extremes and our guide to climate responsive metal facades go deeper. For material comparison, see exterior elevation materials for Indian buildings.

What About South Facing and East Facing Walls?

Every orientation needs a different approach. For south facing walls, horizontal shading works better, as covered in our guide on south facing facade options.

Upkeep Tips for West Facades

Strong sun is hard on finishes and sealants. Wash dust off regularly, check fixings and sealants once a year, and touch up any chips early. See our metal facade maintenance guide.
Common Mistakes

• Relying on horizontal canopies for west sun
  • Using large unprotected glass on the west face
  • Choosing dark colours without considering heat
  • Sealing the wall with no ventilation gap
  • Skipping a proper sun angle study
Frequently Asked Questions

Which direction is worst for heat in India?

West facing walls usually take the hardest heat, because of the low, strong afternoon sun.

What is the best facade for a west facing house?

A ventilated metal facade combined with vertical fins or a perforated screen, and protected glass.

Do vertical fins really help?

Yes. They block low angle sun that horizontal overhangs miss.

Does colour make a difference?

Yes. Lighter colours reflect more heat. Pair them with a quality finish.

Can I add shading to an existing west wall?

Often yes, using a lightweight outer frame or screen. A structural check is needed first.
